how_scores_work: Each version gets up to 100 points: evidence that people have this problem (30 points), fit with your skills, budget and time (25 points), places to reach these customers (20 points), can be built as a first version (15 points), room next to existing options (10 points). These weights are design choices, not facts (config/scoring.toml).

points.Evidence that people have this problem: 19 of 30: Found 4 real examples of people describing this problem or looking for help with it, on graphicdesignforum.com, jenniferbourn.com, rasmussen.edu and webflow.com. Full marks need 5. Of these, 2 are people describing it first-hand or asking for help; 2 are articles or other pages (these count a little less); 3 of 4 are about your market (the others count less). For example: “Freelance designers often feel frustrated when clients send last‑minute changes and ask why work isn’t finished yet” / “Freelance designers feel confused when clients keep changing their mind and add work, making it hard to set clear expectations”.

problem_claims: Freelance designers are looking for free contract templates that protect both designers and clients.
Freelance designers struggle with scope creep, making it hard to finish on time and get paid properly.
Freelance designers need a contract to protect their rights and ensure payment
Freelance designers often feel frustrated when clients send last‑minute changes and ask why work isn’t finished yet.
Freelance designers feel confused when clients keep changing their mind and add work, making it hard to set clear expectations.
Designers worry that without a clear vision of client expectations they cannot tell if they are meeting client needs.
Freelance graphic designers make common onboarding mistakes such as unclear briefs and contracts.
Freelancers are looking for step‑by‑step onboarding templates to streamline new client setup.
